441	/* Find a record-capable and a playback-capable node under /dev/audio.
442	 *
443	 * Done by capability rather than by name: the device names come from the
444	 * board's audio registration, which lives in the VM board tree, and a wrong
445	 * guess would present as ENOENT at run time for no good reason.
446	 */
447	
448	static int mic_find_devices(char *inpath, char *outpath, size_t len)
449	{
450	  struct audio_caps_s caps;
451	  struct dirent *entry;
452	  char path[MIC_PATH_MAX];
453	  DIR *dirp;
454	  int found = 0;
455	  int fd;
456	
457	  inpath[0]  = '\0';
458	  outpath[0] = '\0';
459	
460	  dirp = opendir("/dev/audio");
461	  if (dirp == NULL)
462	    {
463	      printf("mic: cannot open /dev/audio: %d\n", errno);
464	      return -errno;
465	    }
466	
467	  while ((entry = readdir(dirp)) != NULL)
468	    {
469	      snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "/dev/audio/%s", entry->d_name);
470	
471	      fd = open(path, O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC);
472	      if (fd < 0)
473	        {
474	          continue;
475	        }
476	
477	      memset(&caps, 0, sizeof(caps));
478	      caps.ac_len     = sizeof(caps);
479	      caps.ac_type    = AUDIO_TYPE_QUERY;
480	      caps.ac_subtype = AUDIO_TYPE_QUERY;
481	
482	      if (ioctl(fd, AUDIOIOC_GETCAPS, (unsigned long)&caps) == caps.ac_len)
483	        {
484	          /* ONE ROLE PER NODE -- an else-if chain, exactly as nxlooper does
485	           * in nxlooper_opendevice().  That is not incidental style.
486	           *
487	           * This board exposes two nodes: /dev/audio/pcm0, which reports BOTH
488	           * directions, and /dev/audio/pcm_in0, which is the record side.
489	           * Treating "reports both" as "usable for both" looks reasonable and
490	           * is wrong -- it claims pcm0 twice, so the capture opens and
491	           * reserves one device through two fds, pcm_in0 is never touched,
492	           * and RX never delivers a single buffer (timed out with 0/32000).
493	           *
494	           * The chain is order-independent here: whichever of the two is
495	           * enumerated first, pcm0 ends up on playback and pcm_in0 on record.
496	           */
497	
498	          if (outpath[0] == '\0' &&
499	              (caps.ac_controls.b[0] & AUDIO_TYPE_OUTPUT) != 0)
500	            {
501	              strlcpy(outpath, path, len);
502	              found++;
503	            }
504	          else if (inpath[0] == '\0' &&
505	                   (caps.ac_controls.b[0] & AUDIO_TYPE_INPUT) != 0)
506	            {
507	              strlcpy(inpath, path, len);
508	              found++;
509	            }
510	        }
511	
512	      close(fd);
513	
514	      if (inpath[0] != '\0' && outpath[0] != '\0')
515	        {
516	          break;
517	        }
518	    }
519	
520	  closedir(dirp);
521	
522	  if (inpath[0] == '\0' || outpath[0] == '\0')
523	    {
524	      printf("mic: need both a record and a playback node "
525	             "(in='%s' out='%s')\n", inpath, outpath);
526	      return -ENODEV;
527	    }
528	
529	  /* Cannot happen with the chain above, but say so loudly rather than hang
530	   * for five seconds if the board ever registers a single full-duplex node.
531	   */
532	
533	  if (strcmp(inpath, outpath) == 0)
534	    {
535	      printf("mic: record and playback resolved to the same node (%s)\n",
536	             inpath);
537	      return -ENODEV;
538	    }
539	
540	  micinfo("mic: record=%s playback=%s\n", inpath, outpath);
541	  return found;
542	}

567	/* Set the ES8311 ADC PGA gain, in dB.  The driver clamps to 0..42 and
568	 * quantises to 6 dB steps (es8311_setmicgain -> ES8311_ADC_REG16).
569	 *
570	 * This MUST be issued AFTER the AUDIO_TYPE_INPUT configure: es8311_configure
571	 * calls es8311_reset(), which hard-writes REG16 = 0x20 and would wipe any
572	 * gain set beforehand.  es8311_start touches REG17 (digital volume) but not
573	 * REG16, so a gain set here survives START.
574	 */
575	
576	static int mic_set_gain(int fd, int db)

578	  struct audio_caps_desc_s desc;

582	  desc.caps.ac_type           = AUDIO_TYPE_FEATURE;
583	  desc.caps.ac_format.hw      = AUDIO_FU_INP_GAIN;
584	  desc.caps.ac_controls.hw[0] = (uint16_t)db;
585	
586	  if (ioctl(fd, AUDIOIOC_CONFIGURE, (unsigned long)&desc) < 0)
587	    {
588	      printf("mic: set gain %d dB failed: %d\n", db, errno);
589	      return -errno;
590	    }

592	  micinfo("mic: ADC gain %d dB\n", db);
593	  return 0;

596	/* Read the DEVICE-level state out of the audio upper half.
597	 *
598	 * AUDIOIOC_GETSTATUS memcpys upper->status, and upper->status->state is the
599	 * exact field that both audio_configure() and audio_start() branch on -- and
600	 * both of them have a silent-success path:
601	 *
602	 *   audio_configure() calls the lower half ONLY when the state is OPEN(0)
603	 *   (for INPUT/OUTPUT types).  Any other state skips the body, leaves ret at
604	 *   OK and returns 0 -- es8311_configure() never runs, so audio_mode keeps
605	 *   whatever es8311_initialize() left it at, which is ES_MODULE_DAC.
606	 *
607	 *   audio_start() calls lower->ops->start ONLY when the state is PREPARED(1)
608	 *   or XRUN(3).  It returns -EPERM for OPEN(0), but for anything else it
609	 *   falls through to "return OK" WITHOUT starting the codec.
610	 *
611	 * Either way the ioctl returns 0 and nothing happens, which is
612	 * indistinguishable from success at the application level.  That is why this
613	 * is measured rather than assumed.
614	 *
615	 * head is the decisive counter: audio_enqueuebuffer() increments
616	 * upper->status->head only AFTER lower->ops->enqueuebuffer() has returned OK,
617	 * so head == nrecbufs proves every record buffer really did land in the
618	 * es8311 pending queue.
619	 *
620	 * With a persistent session these counters are cumulative for the life of the
621	 * session rather than for one capture, so read them as "in flight = head -
622	 * tail", not as absolute numbers.
623	 *
624	 * States: 0 OPEN, 1 PREPARED, 2 PAUSED, 3 XRUN, 4 DRAINING, 5 RUNNING.
625	 */
626	
627	static void mic_status(int fd, const char *tag)
628	{
629	#if MIC_VERBOSE
630	  struct audio_status_s st;
631	
632	  memset(&st, 0, sizeof(st));
633	  if (ioctl(fd, AUDIOIOC_GETSTATUS, (unsigned long)&st) < 0)
634	    {
635	      printf("mic: [%-10s] GETSTATUS failed: %d\n", tag, errno);
636	      return;
637	    }
638	
639	  printf("mic: [%-10s] state=%d head=%lu tail=%lu\n",
640	         tag, st.state, (unsigned long)st.head, (unsigned long)st.tail);
641	#else
642	  (void)fd;
643	  (void)tag;
644	#endif
645	}

666	/* Submit a buffer.  The caller owns apb->nbytes and must set it first: on the
667	 * record side it means "empty, fill me" (0) and on the playback side it means
668	 * "this much data to send" (nmaxbytes).  It is read by the driver during the
669	 * ioctl, so it cannot be fixed up afterwards.
670	 */
671	
672	static int mic_enqueue(int fd, struct ap_buffer_s *apb)
673	{
674	  struct audio_buf_desc_s desc;
675	
676	  memset(&desc, 0, sizeof(desc));
677	  desc.numbytes  = apb->nmaxbytes;
678	  desc.u.buffer  = apb;
679	
680	  if (ioctl(fd, AUDIOIOC_ENQUEUEBUFFER, (unsigned long)&desc) < 0)
681	    {
682	      return -errno;
683	    }
684	
685	  return 0;
686	}
687	
688	/* Wait until nothing is in flight on either device.
689	 *
690	 * A capture stops requeueing the moment it has the samples it asked for, so a
691	 * couple of record buffers are usually still down in the driver at that point.
692	 * They have to come home before the next capture re-enqueues them, otherwise
693	 * that capture would hand the driver a buffer it is already holding.
694	 *
695	 * tail counts completions and head counts accepted enqueues, so tail == head
696	 * on both devices means nothing is in flight.  Bounded, because a wedged
697	 * driver must not hang the shell.
698	 */
699	
700	/* One buffer is 2046 frames = 128 ms of audio, so a full pool takes
701	 * MIC_WANT_BUFS x 128 ms to drain -- 2.3 s at 18 buffers.  The old budget was
702	 * 1 s, sized when the pool was 4, and build 51 blew straight through it: the
703	 * quiesce gave up with most of the pool still held by the driver, capture 2
704	 * armed with only six free buffers, and those six recycled three times over
705	 * inside one window.  The first of them came back with both slots nonzero
706	 * (s=5374 24678 143 14002) and put 26465 into the profile three times.
707	 *
708	 * Sized for the whole pool with headroom.  It is a ceiling, not a cost --
709	 * mic_collect() no longer requeues while fresh buffers remain, so the normal
710	 * case has one buffer in flight and exits on the first pass.
711	 */
712	
713	#define MIC_QUIESCE_TRIES  80      /* x 50 ms = 4 s worst case */
714	
715	static void mic_quiesce(struct mic_ctx_s *ctx)
716	{
717	  struct audio_status_s rst;
718	  struct audio_status_s pst;
719	  struct audio_msg_s msg;
720	  struct timespec deadline;
721	  unsigned int prio;
722	  ssize_t size;
723	  int i;
724	
725	  memset(&rst, 0, sizeof(rst));
726	  memset(&pst, 0, sizeof(pst));
727	
728	  if (!ctx->mq_open)
729	    {
730	      return;
731	    }
732	
733	  for (i = 0; i < MIC_QUIESCE_TRIES; i++)
734	    {
735	      if (ctx->recfd >= 0)
736	        {
737	          ioctl(ctx->recfd, AUDIOIOC_GETSTATUS, (unsigned long)&rst);
738	        }
739	
740	      if (ctx->playfd >= 0)
741	        {
742	          ioctl(ctx->playfd, AUDIOIOC_GETSTATUS, (unsigned long)&pst);
743	        }
744	
745	      if (rst.head == rst.tail && pst.head == pst.tail)
746	        {
747	          break;
748	        }
749	
750	      clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, &deadline);
751	      deadline.tv_nsec += 50 * 1000000;
752	      if (deadline.tv_nsec >= 1000000000)
753	        {
754	          deadline.tv_sec  += 1;
755	          deadline.tv_nsec -= 1000000000;
756	        }
757	
758	      /* A timeout here is not an error -- it just means no buffer came back
759	       * during this slice, so re-read the counters and keep waiting.
760	       */
761	
762	      size = mq_timedreceive(ctx->mq, (char *)&msg, sizeof(msg), &prio,
763	                             &deadline);
764	      (void)size;
765	    }
766	
767	  micinfo("mic: quiesce rec %lu/%lu play %lu/%lu after %d\n",
768	         (unsigned long)rst.tail, (unsigned long)rst.head,
769	         (unsigned long)pst.tail, (unsigned long)pst.head, i);
770	}
771	
772	/* Discard anything still sitting in the message queue.
773	 *
774	 * mic_quiesce() stops as soon as the counters balance, which can leave the
775	 * final DEQUEUE notifications unread.  Those messages carry buffer pointers,
776	 * and a stale one picked up by the NEXT capture would be both wrong data and
777	 * a double enqueue of a buffer we are about to submit ourselves.  So the queue
778	 * is emptied before every capture, using a deadline that has already passed so
779	 * mq_timedreceive returns immediately once it is dry.
780	 */
781	
782	static void mic_flush_mq(struct mic_ctx_s *ctx)
783	{
784	  struct audio_msg_s msg;
785	  struct timespec deadline;
786	  unsigned int prio;
787	  int dropped = 0;
788	
789	  if (!ctx->mq_open)
790	    {
791	      return;
792	    }
793	
794	  for (; ; )
795	    {
796	      clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, &deadline);
797	
798	      if (mq_timedreceive(ctx->mq, (char *)&msg, sizeof(msg), &prio,
799	                          &deadline) != sizeof(msg))
800	        {
801	          break;
802	        }
803	
804	      dropped++;
805	    }
806	
807	  if (dropped > 0)
808	    {
809	      printf("mic: flushed %d stale message(s)\n", dropped);
810	    }
811	}
812	
813	/* Submit every record buffer, plus one buffer of TX silence.
814	 *
815	 * Enqueueing is what actually arms the hardware.  On the record side es8311's
816	 * worker only calls I2S_RECEIVE when it has a buffer, and i2s_rxdma_start()
817	 * only loads a DMA descriptor when one is pending; on the transmit side
818	 * submitting a buffer is what sets I2S_TX_START.  AUDIOIOC_START, already
819	 * issued once at session open, does neither.
820	 *
821	 * TX is re-primed on every capture even though the clock should still be free
822	 * running from the last one -- patch #16 clears I2S_TX_STOP_EN so BCLK/WS do
823	 * not gate off when the FIFO drains.  One 8192-byte buffer is only 256 ms of
824	 * audio and captures are a full second, so the clock demonstrably outlives the
825	 * data; the re-prime costs nothing and removes the assumption.
826	 */
827	
828	static int mic_arm(struct mic_ctx_s *ctx)
829	{
830	  int ret;
831	  int i;
832	
833	  for (i = 0; i < ctx->nrecbufs; i++)
834	    {
835	      ctx->recbufs[i]->nbytes  = 0;
836	      ctx->recbufs[i]->curbyte = 0;
837	
838	      ret = mic_enqueue(ctx->recfd, ctx->recbufs[i]);
839	      if (ret < 0)
840	        {
841	          printf("mic: enqueue record buffer %d failed: %d\n", i, ret);
842	          return ret;
843	        }
844	    }
845	
846	  memset(ctx->playbuf->samp, 0, ctx->playbuf->nmaxbytes);
847	  ctx->playbuf->nbytes  = ctx->playbuf->nmaxbytes;
848	  ctx->playbuf->curbyte = 0;
849	
850	  ret = mic_enqueue(ctx->playfd, ctx->playbuf);
851	  if (ret < 0)
852	    {
853	      printf("mic: priming TX failed: %d\n", ret);
854	      return ret;
855	    }
856	
857	  return 0;
858	}
859	
860	/* Run the ADC power-up transient through and throw it away.  See
861	 * MIC_WARMUP_BUFS.  Failure here is not fatal: a warm-up that times out costs
862	 * a dirty first capture, not a broken session.
863	 */
864	
865	static void mic_warmup(struct mic_ctx_s *ctx)
866	{
867	  struct audio_msg_s msg;
868	  struct timespec deadline;
869	  unsigned int prio;
870	  int discarded = 0;
871	  int guard = 0;
872	
873	  while (discarded < MIC_WARMUP_BUFS && guard++ < MIC_WARMUP_BUFS * 4)
874	    {
875	      struct ap_buffer_s *apb;
876	
877	      clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, &deadline);
878	      deadline.tv_sec += 1;
879	
880	      if (mq_timedreceive(ctx->mq, (char *)&msg, sizeof(msg), &prio,
881	                          &deadline) != sizeof(msg))
882	        {
883	          break;
884	        }
885	
886	      if (msg.msg_id != AUDIO_MSG_DEQUEUE)
887	        {
888	          continue;
889	        }
890	
891	      apb = (struct ap_buffer_s *)msg.u.ptr;
892	      if (apb == NULL || apb == ctx->playbuf)
893	        {
894	          continue;
895	        }
896	
897	      discarded++;
898	      apb->nbytes  = 0;
899	      apb->curbyte = 0;
900	
901	      if (mic_enqueue(ctx->recfd, apb) < 0)
902	        {
903	          break;
904	        }
905	    }
906	
907	  micinfo("mic: warmup discarded %d buffer(s)\n", discarded);
908	}

910	/* Open the devices and leave them RUNNING.  Called once per boot. */
911	
912	static int mic_session_open(struct mic_ctx_s *ctx)
913	{
914	  struct ap_buffer_info_s bufinfo;
915	  struct ap_buffer_info_s playbufinfo;
916	  char inpath[MIC_PATH_MAX];
917	  char outpath[MIC_PATH_MAX];
918	  int ret;
919	  int i;
920	
921	  memset(ctx, 0, sizeof(*ctx));
922	  ctx->recfd  = -1;
923	  ctx->playfd = -1;
924	
925	  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_FIND);
926	  ret = mic_find_devices(inpath, outpath, sizeof(inpath));
927	  if (ret < 0)
928	    {
929	      return ret;
930	    }
931	
932	  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_OPEN_REC);
933	  ctx->recfd = open(inpath, O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC);
934	  if (ctx->recfd < 0)
935	    {
936	      printf("mic: open %s failed: %d\n", inpath, errno);
937	      return -errno;
938	    }
939	
940	  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_OPEN_PLAY);
941	  ctx->playfd = open(outpath, O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC);
942	  if (ctx->playfd < 0)
943	    {
944	      printf("mic: open %s failed: %d\n", outpath, errno);
945	      return -errno;
946	    }
947	
948	  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_RSV_REC);
949	  if (ioctl(ctx->recfd, AUDIOIOC_RESERVE, 0) < 0)
950	    {
951	      printf("mic: reserve record failed: %d\n", errno);
952	      return -errno;
953	    }
954	
955	  ctx->rec_reserved = true;
956	
957	  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_RSV_PLAY);
958	  if (ioctl(ctx->playfd, AUDIOIOC_RESERVE, 0) < 0)
959	    {
960	      printf("mic: reserve playback failed: %d\n", errno);
961	      return -errno;
962	    }
963	
964	  ctx->play_reserved = true;
965	
966	  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_CFG_REC);
967	  ret = mic_configure(ctx->recfd, AUDIO_TYPE_INPUT);
968	  if (ret < 0)
969	    {
970	      return ret;
971	    }
972	
973	  /* Must read state=1 (PREPARED).  If it reads 0 (OPEN), the CONFIGURE was a
974	   * silent no-op and the record node is still in ES_MODULE_DAC -- which sends
975	   * its buffers to I2S_SEND and starves RX exactly as observed.
976	   */
977	
978	  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_ST_REC_CFG);
979	  mic_status(ctx->recfd, "rec cfg");
980	
981	  /* Configured to match the record side.  TX is only ever fed silence here,
982	   * but it generates the clock RX runs on, so its frame geometry has to be
983	   * the same or RX samples at the wrong rate.
984	   */
985	
986	  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_CFG_PLAY);
987	  ret = mic_configure(ctx->playfd, AUDIO_TYPE_OUTPUT);
988	  if (ret < 0)
989	    {
990	      return ret;
991	    }
992	
993	  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_ST_PLY_CFG);
994	  mic_status(ctx->playfd, "play cfg");
995	
996	  /* Gain goes here, after BOTH configures, deliberately.
997	   *
998	   * pcm0 and pcm_in0 are two independent es8311 priv structs driving ONE
999	   * physical codec, and es8311_configure calls es8311_reset() on whichever
1000	   * priv it was handed.  So configuring playback re-resets the chip and
1001	   * would wipe a gain applied straight after the record configure.
1002	   *
1003	   * Disabled by default -- see MIC_GAIN_DB.
1004	   */
1005	
1006	  if (MIC_GAIN_DB >= 0)
1007	    {
1008	      MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_GAIN);
1009	      mic_set_gain(ctx->recfd, MIC_GAIN_DB);
1010	    }
1011	
1012	  /* GETBUFFERINFO is NOT just a query -- it is what arms allocation.
1013	   *
1014	   * audio.c's AUDIOIOC_GETBUFFERINFO handler copies the driver's reply into
1015	   * upper->nbuffers as a side effect, and audio_allocbuffer() opens with
1016	   * "if (upper->periods >= upper->nbuffers) return 0;".  Skip the query on a
1017	   * device and its nbuffers stays 0, so the very first ALLOCBUFFER on it
1018	   * returns 0 -- not a negative errno, literally zero, which reads like
1019	   * success to anything checking for < 0.
1020	   *
1021	   * So it has to be issued on BOTH devices: the counter lives in the
1022	   * per-device upper half, and answering for the record node does nothing for
1023	   * the playback node.  nxlooper does the same, once per device.
1024	   *
1025	   * The reply is reported rather than assumed, because 4 x 8192 happens to be
1026	   * both the es8311 driver's answer and the CONFIG_AUDIO_* fallback below --
1027	   * identical numbers, opposite meanings.
1028	   */
1029	
1030	  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_BUFI_REC);
1031	  ret = ioctl(ctx->recfd, AUDIOIOC_GETBUFFERINFO, (unsigned long)&bufinfo);
1032	  micinfo("mic: record GETBUFFERINFO ret=%d\n", ret);
1033	  if (ret != OK)
1034	    {
1035	      bufinfo.buffer_size = CONFIG_AUDIO_BUFFER_NUMBYTES;
1036	      bufinfo.nbuffers    = CONFIG_AUDIO_NUM_BUFFERS;
1037	    }
1038	
1039	  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_BUFI_PLAY);
1040	  ret = ioctl(ctx->playfd, AUDIOIOC_GETBUFFERINFO,
1041	              (unsigned long)&playbufinfo);
1042	  micinfo("mic: playback GETBUFFERINFO ret=%d\n", ret);
1043	  if (ret != OK)
1044	    {
1045	      playbufinfo.buffer_size = CONFIG_AUDIO_BUFFER_NUMBYTES;
1046	      playbufinfo.nbuffers    = CONFIG_AUDIO_NUM_BUFFERS;
1047	    }
1048	
1049	  /* Deliberately ask for more than the driver suggested -- see MIC_WANT_BUFS.
1050	   * This also widens the message queue below, since mq_maxmsg is derived from
1051	   * this count, which is what a window's worth of un-drained DEQUEUEs needs.
1052	   */
1053	
1054	  if (bufinfo.nbuffers < MIC_WANT_BUFS)
1055	    {
1056	      bufinfo.nbuffers = MIC_WANT_BUFS;
1057	    }
1058	
1059	  if (bufinfo.nbuffers > MIC_MAX_BUFS)
1060	    {
1061	      bufinfo.nbuffers = MIC_MAX_BUFS;
1062	    }
1063	
1064	  printf("mic: %d buffers x %d B\n",
1065	         (int)bufinfo.nbuffers, (int)bufinfo.buffer_size);
1066	
1067	  for (i = 0; i < bufinfo.nbuffers; i++)
1068	    {
1069	      /* Re-stamped every iteration.  The stage does not change, but the
1070	       * sequence number does, so a probe can tell an allocation that is
1071	       * grinding through 18 buffers from one that is wedged on a single
1072	       * ALLOCBUFFER -- which the stage alone cannot.
1073	       */
1074	
1075	      MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_ALLOC_REC);
1076	      ret = mic_alloc_buffer(ctx->recfd, &ctx->recbufs[i],
1077	                             bufinfo.buffer_size);
1078	      if (ret < 0)
1079	        {
1080	          /* Asking past the driver's suggested depth is speculative, so a
1081	           * refusal partway through is a legitimate answer rather than a
1082	           * failure -- carry on with what was granted.  Below the suggested
1083	           * depth it is a real error and still aborts.
1084	           */
1085	
1086	          if (i >= MIC_MIN_BUFS)
1087	            {
1088	              printf("mic: pool capped at %d buffers (wanted %d, ret %d)\n",
1089	                     i, (int)bufinfo.nbuffers, ret);
1090	              break;
1091	            }
1092	
1093	          return ret;
1094	        }
1095	
1096	      ctx->nrecbufs = i + 1;
1097	    }
1098	
1099	  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_ALLOC_PLAY);
1100	  ret = mic_alloc_buffer(ctx->playfd, &ctx->playbuf, playbufinfo.buffer_size);
1101	  if (ret < 0)
1102	    {
1103	      return ret;
1104	    }
1105	
1106	  snprintf(ctx->mqname, sizeof(ctx->mqname), "/vpmic%d", (int)getpid());
1107	
1108	  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_MQ_OPEN);
1109	
1110	  {
1111	    struct mq_attr attr;
1112	
1113	    attr.mq_maxmsg  = bufinfo.nbuffers + 8;
1114	    attr.mq_msgsize = sizeof(struct audio_msg_s);
1115	    attr.mq_curmsgs = 0;
1116	    attr.mq_flags   = 0;
1117	
1118	    ctx->mq = mq_open(ctx->mqname, O_RDWR | O_CREAT, 0644, &attr);
1119	  }
1120	
1121	  if (ctx->mq == (mqd_t)-1)
1122	    {
1123	      printf("mic: mq_open failed: %d\n", errno);
1124	      return -errno;
1125	    }
1126	
1127	  ctx->mq_open = true;
1128	
1129	  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_REG_MQ);
1130	  if (ioctl(ctx->recfd, AUDIOIOC_REGISTERMQ, (unsigned long)ctx->mq) < 0 ||
1131	      ioctl(ctx->playfd, AUDIOIOC_REGISTERMQ, (unsigned long)ctx->mq) < 0)
1132	    {
1133	      printf("mic: REGISTERMQ failed: %d\n", errno);
1134	      return -errno;
1135	    }
1136	
1137	  /* Buffers must be in the driver's hands BEFORE START on this codec: START
1138	   * is what spawns es8311's worker thread, and the worker looks for work in
1139	   * pendq as soon as it runs.  This is the order nxlooper uses and the order
1140	   * every working capture on this board has used.
1141	   */
1142	
1143	  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_ARM);
1144	  ret = mic_arm(ctx);
1145	  if (ret < 0)
1146	    {
1147	      return ret;
1148	    }
1149	
1150	  /* head must equal nrecbufs here.  That is what proves the buffers got past
1151	   * audio_enqueuebuffer() into es8311's pendq.
1152	   */
1153	
1154	  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_ST_ENQ);
1155	  mic_status(ctx->recfd, "rec enq");
1156	  mic_status(ctx->playfd, "play enq");
1157	
1158	  /* TX starts FIRST.  Without a running TX, RX never sees a bit clock and the
1159	   * dequeue loop blocks until the timeout with zero buffers returned -- RX
1160	   * borrows BCLK/WS from TX in full-duplex mode.  See mic.h.
1161	   */
1162	
1163	  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_START_PLAY);
1164	  if (ioctl(ctx->playfd, AUDIOIOC_START, 0) < 0)
1165	    {
1166	      printf("mic: start playback failed: %d\n", errno);
1167	      return -errno;
1168	    }
1169	
1170	  ctx->play_started = true;
1171	
1172	  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_ST_PLY_STA);
1173	  mic_status(ctx->playfd, "play start");
1174	
1175	  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_START_REC);
1176	  if (ioctl(ctx->recfd, AUDIOIOC_START, 0) < 0)
1177	    {
1178	      printf("mic: start record failed: %d\n", errno);
1179	      return -errno;
1180	    }
1181	
1182	  ctx->rec_started = true;
1183	
1184	  /* Must read state=5 (RUNNING).  A state that is neither PREPARED(1) nor
1185	   * XRUN(3) here means audio_start() took its silent fall-through and
1186	   * es8311_start() was never called -- no worker thread, so nothing ever
1187	   * drains pendq into I2S_RECEIVE, which is what "act=0 pend=0" reports.
1188	   */
1189	
1190	  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_ST_REC_STA);
1191	  mic_status(ctx->recfd, "rec start");
1192	
1193	  ctx->open  = true;
1194	  ctx->owner = getpid();
1195	
1196	  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_WARMUP);
1197	  mic_warmup(ctx);
1198	
1199	  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_OPENED);
1200	  return 0;
1201	}

1203	/* Full teardown.  Only on shutdown, or to recover from a failed capture --
1204	 * NOT between successful captures, which is the bug this file exists to fix.
1205	 */
1206	
1207	static void mic_session_close(struct mic_ctx_s *ctx)
1208	{
1209	  struct audio_buf_desc_s desc;
1210	  int i;
1211	
1212	  if (ctx->rec_started)
1213	    {
1214	      ioctl(ctx->recfd, AUDIOIOC_STOP, 0);
1215	    }
1216	
1217	  if (ctx->play_started)
1218	    {
1219	      ioctl(ctx->playfd, AUDIOIOC_STOP, 0);
1220	    }
1221	
1222	  /* Must run after STOP and before FREEBUFFER: freeing a buffer the driver is
1223	   * still holding leaves it pointing at released memory.
1224	   */
1225	
1226	  mic_quiesce(ctx);
1227	
1228	  if (ctx->mq_open)
1229	    {
1230	      if (ctx->recfd >= 0)
1231	        {
1232	          ioctl(ctx->recfd, AUDIOIOC_UNREGISTERMQ, (unsigned long)ctx->mq);
1233	        }
1234	
1235	      if (ctx->playfd >= 0)
1236	        {
1237	          ioctl(ctx->playfd, AUDIOIOC_UNREGISTERMQ, (unsigned long)ctx->mq);
1238	        }
1239	    }
1240	
1241	  for (i = 0; i < ctx->nrecbufs; i++)
1242	    {
1243	      if (ctx->recbufs[i] != NULL)
1244	        {
1245	          memset(&desc, 0, sizeof(desc));
1246	          desc.u.buffer = ctx->recbufs[i];
1247	          ioctl(ctx->recfd, AUDIOIOC_FREEBUFFER, (unsigned long)&desc);
1248	          ctx->recbufs[i] = NULL;
1249	        }
1250	    }
1251	
1252	  if (ctx->playbuf != NULL)
1253	    {
1254	      memset(&desc, 0, sizeof(desc));
1255	      desc.u.buffer = ctx->playbuf;
1256	      ioctl(ctx->playfd, AUDIOIOC_FREEBUFFER, (unsigned long)&desc);
1257	      ctx->playbuf = NULL;
1258	    }
1259	
1260	  if (ctx->rec_reserved)
1261	    {
1262	      ioctl(ctx->recfd, AUDIOIOC_RELEASE, 0);
1263	    }
1264	
1265	  if (ctx->play_reserved)
1266	    {
1267	      ioctl(ctx->playfd, AUDIOIOC_RELEASE, 0);
1268	    }
1269

`lasterr -110` is `-ETIMEDOUT`, and the stage counter pins it exactly. Counting `MIC_STAGE()` calls for a first-capture-of-boot with an 18-buffer pool:

`ENTER`=1 … `BUFI_PLAY`=13, `ALLOC_REC`×18 = 14–31, `ALLOC_PLAY`=32, `MQ_OPEN`=33 … `OPENED`=42, then `COLLECT`=43, `QUIESCE`=44, **`CLOSE`=45**.

seq 45 is `CLOSE` to the digit. (b65's 22 buffers gave 49 — +4, same arithmetic.) So the session opened completely and correctly, and then [mic.c:1656](app/velapaw/voice/mic.c#L1656) `mic_collect()` timed out.

That kills my "over the buffer ceiling" story for good, because b66 asks for 16000 against a 17391 ceiling — the same request b62 served. Which leaves exactly one functional difference between b62 and b66 in the entire capture path:

| | b62 (worked) | b66 |
|---|---|---|
| samples | 16000 | 16000 |
| pool / skip | 18 / 1 | 18 / 1 |
| **capture timeout** | **8000 ms** | **5000 ms** |

Everything else I changed — `voice_align`, the vote rule, `lasterr`, the `#error` guard — is downstream of the capture or compile-time only. I tightened that timeout in b66 for no reason other than tidiness, and the first capture of a boot is the one that carries the codec's ADC power-up. That's what `MIC_WARMUP_BUFS` exists for.

Before I spend a build on that, there's a free experiment that splits the question in half.

**On the next cold boot, before opening any dialog, run `velapaw kws mic 1` at the nsh prompt.**

That path calls the identical `mic_collect()` with its own timeout, and it has worked on every build including this one's ancestors. So:

- **It captures fine** → collect is healthy in b66, and the worker's 5000 ms budget is the whole bug. One-character fix.
- **It also times out** → the regression is in mic.c or the board, not the worker, and I've been looking in the wrong file for three builds.

Cold unplug/replug first — the board is wedged in `mic_session_close()` again, and only a power cycle clears that. Then `velapaw kws mic 1` as the *first* thing, no dialog.

Meanwhile I'll make the two changes I already owe, so the build is ready the moment you report.

int velapaw_mic_last_error(void);

/* What the driver's counters read at the moment a capture gave up.
 *
 * -110 says the collect timed out; it does not say whether RX never started,
 * started and stalled, or ran normally into a buffer pool that could not cover
 * the request.  Those want completely different fixes and the counters
 * separate them outright:
 *
 *   rhead   should equal the pool depth -- proof every buffer was accepted
 *           into es8311's pendq.  Short means arming failed, not receiving.
 *   rtail   completions.  0 means RX never delivered ONE buffer, i.e. no bit
 *           clock or no worker thread; the codec never ran at all.
 *   seq     buffers accepted into this window (after MIC_SKIP_BUFS).  Nonzero
 *           with a short got means delivery is working but too slow -- a
 *           timeout that a longer budget would have survived.
 *   phase   -1 means every buffer that did arrive was zero to the bit, so RX
 *           is running and the microphone side is dead.  See mic_data_phase().
 *
 * Read this together with velapaw_mic_stage(): the stage says where the code
 * stopped, these say what the hardware was doing when it did.  Published from
 * inside mic_collect() before the teardown, for the same reason the errno is.
 */

struct velapaw_mic_fail_s
{
  unsigned long got;    /* output bytes collected when the capture gave up */
  unsigned long want;   /* output bytes it was asked for                   */
  unsigned long rhead;  /* record enqueues the driver accepted             */

Fair enough — here's my read on it, since it's worth deciding before you act on it.

**The central claim is contradicted by our own history.** If the GDMA descriptor chain never fired `suc_eof`, no capture would ever have completed on this board. But they have, repeatedly: `yes` 0.996 and `no` 0.750 on build 52, and b62's whole run of live scores (eight 0.441/0.176/0.316, one 0.762) came from real captured audio with real energy profiles. A static descriptor-construction bug doesn't work on Tuesday and fail on Thursday — and nothing in the driver changed between b62 and b66. Only the app did.

**Our own RXDUMP says the opposite of "no interrupts fire".** That `eofnum=0x0ffc` reading is 4092 bytes, and 4092-bytes-per-delivery is the number the entire de-interleaving path in [mic.c](app/velapaw/voice/mic.c) is built around — `MIC_STRIDE`, the 1023-samples-per-buffer arithmetic, all of it. EOF fires, and it fires at a specific, repeatable, correct count. The `d[0]=0xff0` + `d[1]=0x10` split is the chain being *traversed*, not stalled.

**Patch #16 is the wrong patch.** It clears `I2S_TX_STOP_EN` so BCLK/WS keep running after the TX FIFO drains — that's the TX clock-gating fix, documented at [mic.h:41-43](app/velapaw/voice/mic.h#L41-L43). It doesn't build descriptor chains. Whatever patch does, it isn't that one.

**Two readings of the log are off:**

- `lastret -999` isn't "the collection loop never completed a cycle." It's my own sentinel, and it means `velapaw_mic_capture()` **never returned** — `g_voice_lastret = got` is the line *after* the call. That distinction is the whole reason the worker is permanently dead rather than just failing.
- "opens a session every few seconds and consistently times out" — the probe says `caps 1`. **One** capture, ever. The three later `dialog start` entries never reached a capture at all; they hit "mic never became ready" because the worker was already gone. Sessions aren't being retried in a loop.

**And the arithmetic in the fix doesn't fit.** `0x3fcbb2d0 − 0x3fcbb280` is 0x50, 80 bytes. An ESP32-S3 GDMA descriptor is 12 bytes, so an 80-byte slip isn't a descriptor stride — it doesn't look like a chain that's off by one element. (I can't check the dump itself, so hold that one loosely.)

---

What I'd keep from it: the *area* is right. My evidence also points at RX arming, and specifically at the **first arm of a session** — that's the capture that failed, every time, in b64/b65/b66. Where I part company is the mechanism: a permanent descriptor fault can't produce an intermittent symptom, so if the descriptors are involved it's about how they're armed the first time, not a wrong constant in the chain.

The good news is we don't have to argue it. b67's counters decide it in one reading:

| probe line | verdict |
|---|---|
| `mic fail rec 0/18` | RX delivered **nothing**. This supports the DMA-stall theory — go to the driver. |
| `mic fail rec 14/18  seq 13` | Delivery worked, just slower than the budget. Driver is fine; the timeout was the bug. |
| `phase -1` | Buffers arrived, all zeros. RX fine, mic side dead. |

That's precisely why I put those counters in this build instead of shipping the timeout fix alone. Let me know what the build says and what `velapaw kws mic 1` does on a cold boot.

Decisive. Look at these two lines together:

```

```

`rec 0/18` — all eighteen record buffers were **accepted** by the driver (`head 18`) and **not one came back** (`tail 0`). `play 1/1` — the TX silence buffer went out and completed. So the bit clock is running, TX is fine, and RX never armed at all. `phase -1` and `got 0` follow from that: zero buffers means zero samples.

That is character-for-character the build-42 signature documented at the top of [mic.c:20-22](app/velapaw/voice/mic.c#L20-L22):

```
build 42 run 2:  mic: timed out with 0/32000 bytes
                 [rec t/out] state=5 head=4 tail=0
                 [play t/out] state=5 head=1 tail=1   <- TX is fine
```

**And the GDMA-descriptor theory is now conclusively dead.** Twenty seconds before that failure, in the same boot, on the same descriptors, `velapaw kws mic 1` captured 16000 samples cleanly — `live slot 0 of 2`, a full profile. Descriptors that deliver 16000 samples and then deliver zero are not misaligned descriptors.

**One caveat about my own experiment:** `seq 91` (not 45) means the worker's session was the *second* of the boot — my `velapaw kws mic 1` opened, captured, and tore down a session first. So this particular run reproduced the known reopen bug, which I partly caused. That doesn't rescue the theory, though: in b64/b65/b66 the worker failed at `seq 45`, as the **first** session of the boot, with nothing before it. Two different paths into the same dead RX.

What they share is the thing mic.c already warns about — [mic.c:604-613](app/velapaw/voice/mic.c#L604-L613):

> `audio_configure()` calls the lower half ONLY when the state is OPEN(0)… Any other state skips the body, leaves ret at OK and returns 0 — `es8311_configure()` never runs, so audio_mode keeps whatever `es8311_initialize()` left it at, which is **ES_MODULE_DAC**.

A record node stuck in DAC mode sends its buffers to `I2S_SEND` instead of `I2S_RECEIVE`. Enqueues are accepted, nothing is ever received. `head 18, tail 0`. That is the observed reading exactly.

The code already knows to check this — `mic_status()` reads the state and asserts it must be 1 (PREPARED) after configure and 5 (RUNNING) after start. But it's compiled to nothing at `MIC_VERBOSE 0`, so we've never seen those numbers. Let me publish them.

void velapaw_mic_last_fail(struct velapaw_mic_fail_s *out);

/* The device states observed while opening a session, for the last two
 * sessions opened.
 *
 * Two, not one, because the interesting comparison is between a session that
 * worked and one that did not, and the cheapest way to get both is one boot
 * where `velapaw kws mic 1` runs before the UI's worker does.  A single
 * reading would only say what the failing session looked like; a pair says
 * what it looked like DIFFERENTLY.
 *
 * The numbers to read, from audio.c:
 *
 *   rec_cfg    MUST be 1 (PREPARED).  0 (OPEN) would mean the ioctl succeeded
 *              without doing anything -- audio_configure() only calls the
 *              lower half from state OPEN and otherwise falls through with
 *              ret = OK -- leaving the record node in ES_MODULE_DAC, where it
 *              sends record buffers to I2S_SEND and RX is never armed.  That
 *              produces head = pool depth with tail = 0, which is exactly what
 *              build 67 measured.
 *   rec_start  MUST be 5 (RUNNING).  Anything else means audio_start() took
 *              the same silent fall-through and es8311_start() never ran, so
 *              there is no worker thread to drain pendq into I2S_RECEIVE.
 *   play_start MUST be 5 as well; TX is what generates the clock RX borrows.
 *
 * States: 0 OPEN, 1 PREPARED, 2 PAUSED, 3 XRUN, 4 DRAINING, 5 RUNNING.
 * A negative value means the GETSTATUS ioctl itself failed.
 */

struct velapaw_mic_open_s
{
  int      pid;         /* task that opened this session                    */
  int      rec_cfg;     /* record state after AUDIOIOC_CONFIGURE            */
  int      rec_start;   /* record state after AUDIOIOC_START                */
  int      play_start;  /* playback state after AUDIOIOC_START              */
  int      nbufs;       /* record buffers actually granted                  */
  int      ret;         /* 0 if the open completed, else where it stopped   */
  unsigned seq;         /* stage sequence at entry, to order the sessions   */
};

/* Fills up to max entries, oldest first, and returns how many were written. */

int velapaw_mic_open_log(struct velapaw_mic_open_s *out, int max);

Two other things in that transcript matter a great deal.

**The model is fine.** `eight (0.941)` — peak 8202, rms 1344, a profile with speech spread across four segments. Against b62's 0.441 / 0.176 / 0.316 for the same word, that's not a marginal improvement, it's a different regime. The weak scores were never the model or the thresholds; they were capture quality. Once the worker can capture at this level, the 0.55 hour gate is not even close to binding, and the vote rule becomes a safety net rather than the fix.

**The difference is the caller, not the session.** Look at the pids:

```
open0 pid 11 seq 1    <- nsh child. RX arms.
open1 pid  4 seq 47   <- the UI's voice worker. RX never arms.
```

Same code, same config, same states, same 18 buffers — and `rec 0/18` with `play 1/1`. The record buffers reach es8311's pending queue and its record worker thread never drains one into `I2S_RECEIVE`, while the *playback* worker completes its buffer normally. That's not configuration. That's the record worker thread not running.

Which makes the caller's scheduling priority the obvious thing to look at, since pid 4 is a thread of the continuously-rendering LVGL task:

`reccfg 1 / recstart 5 / playstart 5` on both. Configuration is not the difference. That theory's dead — I'll stop pushing it.

Two things from this run are worth more than the failure was.

**The model is not the problem, and never was.** `eight (0.941)`, peak 8202, rms 1344, energy spread across four segments. Compare b62's readings for the same word: 0.441, 0.176, 0.316. That's not tuning distance, that's a different signal. Every threshold argument we've had — the 0.55 hour gate, the vote rule, the alignment window — was downstream of captures that were quiet and badly framed. At this level the hour gate isn't remotely binding.

**And the failure is caller-specific.** Same code, same states, same 18 buffers:

```
open0 pid 11 (nsh child)          RX arms, 16000 samples, eight 0.941
open1 pid  4 (UI voice worker)    rec 0/18 — head 18, tail 0
```

`head 18` means es8311's `enqueuebuffer` accepted every one into its pending queue. `tail 0` means its **record worker thread never drained a single one** into `I2S_RECEIVE`. Meanwhile `play 1/1` — the *playback* worker, created moments earlier in the same session by the same caller, completed its buffer fine.

That reframes the hang, too. `mic_session_close()` starts with `ioctl(AUDIOIOC_STOP)`, and `es8311_stop()` signals the worker thread and **joins** it. A record worker that is stuck is exactly a worker that can't be joined — so:

> the record worker never runs → `tail 0` → collect times out → `STOP` blocks joining that worker → `mic_session_close()` hangs → the voice worker is gone for the boot

One stuck thread explains `tail 0`, the `-110`, *and* the permanent wedge. That's the first theory I've had that accounts for all three instead of just one.

There's a free way to test it, and build 42 already used it. On the next cold boot:

1. Open the dialog, let it fail (**no** `velapaw kws mic` this time — one session only, so it matches the b66 case)
2. At the prompt: **`ps`**

What I'm looking for in that listing:

| what `ps` shows | meaning |
|---|---|
| an es8311 worker thread, blocked | it exists and is stuck — and *where* it's blocked names the bug |
| **no** es8311 record thread at all | `es8311_start()` reported RUNNING but never created the worker. That's a driver bug I can point at precisely. |
| a record thread running normally | my theory's wrong again and the problem is between the worker and I2S |

Build 42's `ps` in this exact state showed *no es8311 threads*, which is why the persistent session was built to avoid teardowns. If that's what we see again, it's the same bug reached by a different road — and this time we'd know it depends on which task called `START`.

**Step 1 is the meal step.** It only accepts *one*, *two*, or *three*. You said "eight" — which the model nailed at **0.957** — and the decoder correctly found nothing matching in a three-word subset that doesn't contain it. Same with "six" at 0.750. The hour comes at step *2*; "eight" is the right word one step later.

So nothing is broken here. Recognition on hardware is now 0.957 and 0.750 on the words you actually spoke, which is far better than anything this project has measured.

**Try again and say "two" first.** Then "eight" when it asks for the hour, then "yes". That's the whole dialog end-to-end with no build.

That said, this exposed a real design fault that I'd like to fix regardless of how the retry goes. The step heard you clearly, knew it heard "eight", and told you only "please repeat" — while the log line it wrote for itself (`one 0.000`) is a number with no meaning, the best of a subset that never contained your word. The user gets silence where the system has the exact answer:

> heard "eight" — say one, two or three

That's a small change in `vsched_step` — the unconstrained result `r` is already in hand, it's what produces the `heard eight 0.957` line. When the confident unconstrained label isn't in the step's subset, say which word was heard and which are expected, instead of the generic retry. It costs nothing at runtime and turns the most likely user error into a self-correcting one.

11	`apps/examples/velapaw/voice/mic.c` — 1 s of 16 kHz mono for `micro_speech`.
12	
13	**WORKING on hardware, build 52 (2026-08-05):** live "yes" **0.996**, "no"
14	**0.750**, silence correctly rejected. Every earlier result was weak
15	(b46: yes 0.539, no 0.715) because of the two defects below, both in capture,
16	neither in the model.
17	
18	## 🔴 RX delivers TWO slots and one of them is dead
19	
20	`I2S_RX_MONO` marks the second slot invalid but does **not** remove it from
21	the stream — both slots reach the FIFO and the DMA, with the invalid one
22	zero-filled. Buffers read `[sample, 0, sample, 0, ...]`. This is not 32-bit
23	slot padding: `i2s_set_datawidth()` programs 16-bit slots
24	(`CHAN_BITS = HALF_SAMPLE_BITS = data_width`). It is VelaPaw patch #25:
25	`TOT_CHAN_NUM=1` (two slots) + `CHAN0_EN|CHAN1_EN` + `I2S_RX_MONO`.
26	
27	Consequence: a 16000-`int16` window was **0.5 s of audio with a zero between
28	every sample** — a mirrored spectrum landing inside micro_speech's mel bins.
29	Fix is `MIC_STRIDE 2` — keep one `int16` in two, in `mic_collect()`.
30	
31	### ⚠️ The live slot flips PER CAPTURE, not per build
32	
33	Build 52, one boot: capture 1 slot 0, capture 2 slot 0, capture 3 **slot 1**.
34	Every capture re-arms RX and the first sample lands wherever the frame is.
35	Hardcoding slot 0 makes a capture come back all zeros and look like a dead
36	mic. `mic_data_phase()` measures it, per capture, by counting **exact zeros**
37	— the dead slot is 0 to the bit while the live slot has an ADC noise floor
38	even in a silent room. It returns −1 for an all-zero buffer (RX emits a few
39	while warming up) so the phase is settled off the first buffer with content,
40	not a coin flip.
41	
42	## 🔴 Audio buffers live in PSRAM and the driver does no cache maintenance
43	
44	`apb->samp` addresses are `0x3C5x_xxxx` = the external-memory window
45	(`CONFIG_ESP32S3_SPIRAM=y`, `CONFIG_MM_REGIONS=2`). `esp32s3_i2s.c` has **no**
46	invalidate/writeback/barrier anywhere. So **reusing a buffer inside one
47	window returns a stale cached copy**: first delivery misses cache and reads
48	what DMA wrote, the copy pulls 4 KB into DCache, and ~500 ms later the same
49	buffer hits those warm lines. Signature: an 8-segment profile that repeats
50	with a period equal to the pool depth, and identical samples at the same
51	`apb` pointer.
52	
53	**Fix = never reuse a buffer inside a window.** `GETBUFFERINFO`'s `nbuffers`
54	is a *suggestion*, not a cap — `ALLOCBUFFER` is per-call. `MIC_WANT_BUFS 18`
55	(one delivery = 4092 B = 2046 `int16` = 1023 usable samples after stride, so
56	16000 needs 16 + `MIC_SKIP_BUFS`).
57	
58	### The follow-on trap: a deep pool overruns the quiesce budget
59	
60	Requeueing every accepted buffer left ~17 in flight; one buffer is 128 ms, so
61	draining needs 2.3 s against a 1 s budget sized when the pool was 4. Quiesce
62	timed out, the *next* capture armed with 6 free buffers, and they recycled 3×
63	— reintroducing the cache bug. Two fixes together:
64	- requeue only when `skipped + seq >= nrecbufs - 1` (self-adjusting: a capped
65	  pool still finishes by falling back to recycling)
66	- `MIC_QUIESCE_TRIES 80` (4 s) — a ceiling, not a cost
67	
68	## The repeat-capture bug was PROCESS EXIT, not I2S
69	
70	Each `velapaw kws mic` is a **separate builtin task**. Flat build, so statics
71	(`g_mic`) survive, but **fds do not** — NuttX closes them at task exit, so run
72	2 found `open == true` and got **`-9` (EBADF)**. Guard the session with the
73	owning pid; if `g_mic.owner != getpid()`, `memset` and reopen — **never
74	`close()` those fds**, the numbers belong to someone else now. Test repeat
75	capture *in one process* (`velapaw kws mic [reps]`); the product captures from
76	the long-lived UI task, which does not exit.
77	
78	Signatures: `es8311_getcoeff`/`setsamplerate` spam **at the nsh prompt between
79	runs** = the kernel closing the devices. `ps` showing no `es8311` threads after
80	a "failed" run = the task is gone, nothing leaked.
81	
82	## ⏳ STILL OPEN: `-110` on session reopen
83	
84	A second `velapaw kws mic` in the same boot times out with `0/32000 bytes`.
85	Reliable, not intermittent — reproduced on builds 48–52. **Only a cold power
86	cycle clears it** (RTS reset does not). Not product-blocking: the feeder holds
87	one session in the long-lived UI task. **Test one `velapaw kws mic 3` per
88	boot.**
89	
90	## Session shape
91	
92	Open, configure, `AUDIOIOC_START` **once**; each capture only enqueues and
93	collects. Between captures the session is running but idle. Free-running RX is
94	not an option: `mq_maxmsg = nbuffers + 8`, so with no reader the driver's
95	`mq_send` would drop buffer pointers. `mic_flush_mq()` before each re-arm.
96	
97	⚠️ **`apb->nbytes` is read by the driver *during* the enqueue ioctl** — the
98	caller sets it: record side `0`, playback side `nmaxbytes`. Zeroing it in a
99	shared helper silently sends a zero-length TX buffer → no clock → hang. TX
100	must stay primed; RX borrows BCLK/WS from TX (see [[velapaw-audio-bringup]]).
101	
102	## Measurement, not ears
103	
104	`velapaw_mic_stats()` prints `peak N@index`, `rms`, `dc`, `rail` and an
105	8-segment peak profile. Reference at 30 dB, build 52, de-interleaved:
106	
107	    silence  rms  26  profile    87    82    87    68    55    67    56    60
108	    "yes"    rms 645  profile   447    90   107   100  4085  5019  1426  1724
109	    "no"     rms 791  profile  1949  5402  3534   596    74    66    87    94
110	
111	`MIC_TRACE` (default 0) prints one line per buffer with the `apb` pointer and
112	four samples — the check on both fixes at once: pointers must all be distinct,
113	`s` must alternate live/0. Turn it on for any future capture regression.
114	Do **not** read a full-scale spike at a fixed index as clipping — that is the
115	start-of-stream transient, see [[velapaw-audio-gain]].

Build 67/68 (2026-08-06): running `velapaw kws mic 1` and *then* opening the
voice dialog puts the UI worker's session into exactly this state —

not a free warm-up. Head 18 / tail 0 = every buffer reached es8311's pendq and
none came back — that pair is the signature, distinct from a real timeout.

for the rest of the boot. Restoring 8000 in b67 fixed it and 72 consecutive
captures have since succeeded.

nowhere near either budget. Something about the first collect after a session
open is far slower than the ones after it. Don't "optimise" this number again

---

description: "VelaPaw voice meal-scheduling dialog — WORKING end to end on hardware (COMMIT meal 2 = 08:00). Hardware-confirmed thresholds, why the score is never renormalised, and the vote rule that turned out to be a safety net"

The MEAL → HOUR → CONFIRM spoken dialog in the edit-pet modal
(`vsched_*` in `app/velapaw/ui/ui_lvgl.c`), on the 14-label tiny_conv KWS
model. **WORKING end to end on hardware, build 68 (2026-08-06):**

    heard two 0.773    -> step2
    heard eight 0.938  -> step3
    heard yes 0.957    -> COMMIT meal 2 = 08:00

**9.6 s, three steps, two retries, zero false accepts.** See
[[velapaw-mic-capture]] for the capture path underneath it.

## Constrained decode — threshold the RAW softmax, never renormalised

Each step knows its legal answers (MEAL `{one,two,three}`, HOUR `{zero..nine}`,
CONFIRM `{yes,no}`) and `velapaw_kws_best_of()` takes the argmax over just
those. **The score returned is the raw probability, deliberately not
renormalised over the subset** — the mass sitting on `_silence_`/`_unknown_`
is exactly the mass meaning "that wasn't one of my words". Renormalising lets
86% of silence/OOV clips through the confirm step; the raw score, 4.9%.

Confirmed live: the model heard `eight 0.957` at the MEAL step and best-of
returned `one 0.000`. That is the design working, not a bug.

## Thresholds (hardware-tuned, build 56; still correct at b68)

    MEAL 0.40    HOUR 0.55    CONFIRM 0.55    TIMEOUT 15000 ms    TRIES 5

They came *down* from 0.45/0.73/0.59 because words through the ES8311 score
0.68–0.71 when correctly heard, not the ~0.99 the test split suggested.
A wrong hour is cheap (CONFIRM reads it back); a *rejected* hour is expensive
(burns a try, ends with nothing set).

## The vote rule is a safety net, not the mechanism

`VSCHED_VOTES 2` + `VSCHED_VOTE_FLOOR 0.25` — a step also accepts a word it
heard twice below threshold. Votes, **not** a consecutive run (the b62 log that
motivated it had the repeats interrupted by a 0.176 reading). MEAL and HOUR
only; CONFIRM keeps the threshold alone since agreeing twice on a two-way
choice is as surprising as a coin landing the same way twice.

In the successful b68 run **`v` never got past 0** — all three accepts cleared
their threshold outright. Keep it for the marginal case; don't tune against it.

## 🔴 The UX fault that cost a whole test session

An owner who answers MEAL with an hour ("eight") got only "say again" — the
subset decode is blind to everything outside the step, so the dialog *had* the
answer at 0.957 and didn't pass it on. Build 69 adds `S_VC_WRONG_FMT`:
when the **unconstrained** winner is a real word, illegal here, and scores
≥ `VSCHED_WRONG_SCORE 0.60`, say `heard "eight" - say 1 / 2 / 3`.

0.60 sits **above** the 0.40/0.55 accept gates on purpose: this message makes a
claim about speech we chose *not* to act on, so it needs more evidence than
acting would, not less.

## Rejections are supposed to happen

Both retries in the good run were correct rejections of bad windows
(`silence 0.324` → `six 0.129`; `six 0.395` → `yes 0.223`). Don't chase them.
For a device that commits a feeding schedule, no-false-accept is the property
that matters — see also the deliberate choice in `vsched_commit()` to write the
modal's **scratch** copy, so voice never bypasses the Save/Cancel buttons.

**Two changes:**

**1. A second, lower-confidence hint** ([ui_lvgl.c](app/velapaw/ui/ui_lvgl.c), `VSCHED_NOTONE_SCORE 0.15`). When no legal answer holds real mass, the modal says `say one of:  1 / 2 / 3` without guessing at what you said. On your last run this would have fired on t1 and t2 — the two the naming rule couldn't reach.

The gate sits at **0.15**, at the *bottom* of the gap in your data, not the middle:

```
legal word, heard weakly   0.215  0.266  0.355  0.395  0.406
said something else        0.000 ... 0.078  0.105  0.141
```

0.141 is the one that worries me — I don't know what was actually spoken for that capture, so it may be a legal word that would now get a confusing hint. Placing the gate low costs a few missed hints and avoids that. It's written into the comment so the next person tuning it knows the margin is thinner than the table suggests.

`_silence_` is excluded — when the model is sure it heard nothing, "say one of 1 / 2 / 3" is the wrong advice and "say again" is right. `_unknown_` is *not* excluded: "a word I don't know" is precisely this case.

**2. `vsched_extend()`** — showing a hint restarts the 15 s clock. The window to act on instructions starts when the instructions appear. `VSCHED_TRIES` still counts every capture, so five bad ones end the step regardless; this can't stretch into an unbounded dialog.

**Test:** cold boot, no `velapaw kws mic`, say **"eight"** at the meal step two or three times. Expect `off-vocab` lines on the weak ones and `wrong word` on any that break 0.60 — and no timeout while you're reading. Then "two"/"eight"/"yes" to confirm the happy path.
while that builds what is the threshold of correct word?

The accept gates, and what a correctly-spoken word actually has to clear:

| step | one capture | or, two agreeing captures | effective floor |
|---|---|---|---|
| MEAL `{one,two,three}` | **0.40** | 0.25 each | **0.25** |
| HOUR `{zero..nine}` | **0.55** | 0.25 each | **0.25** |
| CONFIRM `{yes,no}` | **0.55** | — no vote path | **0.55** |

So a correct word needs 0.40/0.55/0.55 in one shot, or — for MEAL and HOUR only — 0.25 twice on independent captures. CONFIRM is the one hard gate, deliberately: it's the last thing before the schedule is written, and agreeing twice on a two-way choice is only as surprising as a coin landing the same way twice.

That's the rule. What matters more is that **correctly-heard words score all over the place** through this microphone:

```
yes    0.957  0.762  0.668
eight  0.957  0.938  0.574  0.488  0.441  0.316  0.266  0.176
two    0.773  0.406  0.355
one    0.680
```

Roughly 0.18 to 0.96 for words that were spoken correctly and identified correctly. The median is somewhere near 0.5 — which is *below* the HOUR gate. That single fact is why the vote rule exists and why it isn't optional: a bare 0.55 gate rejects about half of correctly-spoken hours, and your b69 run is a worked example — 0.395, then 0.266, both correct, both rejected, recovered only by agreement.

For contrast, the two hint gates in b70 run the other way:

- **0.60** to name a word (`heard "eight"`) — above every accept gate, because claiming what you said is a stronger claim than acting on it.
- **0.15** on the *constrained* score to say `say one of: 1 / 2 / 3` — the weakest claim, so the lowest bar.

One caveat on all these numbers: they're raw softmax over 14 categories, never renormalised over the step's subset. A "0.40" here is not 40% confidence that you said *two* — it's 40% of the total mass sitting on *two* while `_unknown_` and `_silence_` keep theirs. That retained mass is exactly what makes a low absolute number still meaningful, and it's why the thresholds look surprisingly low for a system that has to be right.

The `mic_session_close()` hang is real and this is it firing.** `lastret -999` means the capture call never returned, and `mic stage 32` says the worker is sitting in session-close — long past the 4 s quiesce ceiling. That's the latent trap from the backlog, no longer latent. It's why one bad capture kills voice for the whole boot instead of costing you one retry.

`play 1/1` is the number I want to understand — TX enqueued once, returned once, never requeued. RX borrows BCLK/WS from TX on this part, so if TX stops the clock stops and RX stalls forever. That would explain one silent buffer and then nothing. Checking rather than guessing:

## 🔴 OPEN: the first capture of a boot intermittently stalls

Signature (b70, and identically b66):

    caps 1  lastret -999   lasterr -110   mic stage 32 (session-close)
    mic open0 pid 4 seq 1 ... bufs 18  ret 0     <- one session, opened fine
    mic fail got 0/32000  phase -1
    mic fail rec 1/19  play 1/1 (tail/head)

RX accepted 19 enqueues and returned **one** buffer, which was silent. TX was
enqueued once, returned once, never requeued — and RX borrows BCLK/WS from TX
on this part, so a dead TX means a dead clock and RX stalls forever. Unproven
but it fits every counter.

⚠️ **`VOICE_CAPTURE_MS` 8000 is NOT the fix.** b66 failed at 5000, b67 restored
8000, three clean boots followed and it looked solved — then b70 failed at 8000
with the same counters. That was three lucky boots, not a fix. The tightening
was never the cause. Don't rely on this number.

### The failure is terminal for the boot, twice over

- `mic_session_close()` **hangs** — `lastret -999` means the capture call never
  returned. `g_mic_busy` is cleared only after close returns, so every later
  caller gets `-EBUSY`. `mic_quiesce()` is bounded (80 × 50 ms) and cannot be
  it; suspicion is the first `AUDIOIOC_STOP` waiting on a driver worker parked
  on a DMA completion that never comes.
- Even without the hang, the voice worker does `g_voice_fail = 1; return NULL;`
  on any negative capture, so one bad capture disables voice for the boot.

🔴 **`MIC_STAGE_CLOSE` (32) is set once on entry and covers two
`AUDIOIOC_STOP`s, the quiesce, `UNREGISTERMQ`, 19 `FREEBUFFER`s, `RELEASE` and
two `close()`s.** No marker inside. Diagnosing the hang needs per-ioctl stages
in `mic_session_close()` first — that instrumentation does not exist yet.


**TX was enqueued once, came back once, and was never re-enqueued.** Your own memory note on this path says it plainly: *"TX must stay primed; RX borrows BCLK/WS from TX."* On this part the receiver has no clock of its own — it runs off the transmitter's BCLK/WS. So the moment the playback buffer returned and wasn't requeued, the bit clock stopped, and RX froze holding the one buffer it had already latched. Everything downstream follows from that: es8311's workers go idle with nothing to deliver, and our thread blocks forever in the close path waiting for a stream that will never move again.

So the question isn't "why did RX stall" — RX stalling is the *consequence*. The question is **why the TX requeue didn't happen**. Let me read that path.

```c
/* A playback buffer coming back is the primed silence completing.

if (apb == ctx->playbuf) { continue; }
```

> *"patch #16 clears I2S_TX_STOP_EN so BCLK/WS do not gate off when the FIFO drains. One 8192-byte buffer is only 256 ms of audio and captures are a full second, so the clock demonstrably outlives the data."*

So TX is primed **once**, with 256 ms of silence, and the capture needs ~1 s of clock. For the remaining ~750 ms the bit clock is running only because patch #16 is assumed to keep it free-running with an empty FIFO. That assumption has never been directly verified — it was inferred from captures succeeding. `play 1/1` is that assumption's failure mode written out: TX drained, returned, and was never re-primed by design.

One honest caveat before I act on it. The timing doesn't line up perfectly: one RX buffer is ~128 ms, so RX died at ~128 ms while TX still had ~128 ms of data left to clock out. If the clock had simply run dry at 256 ms I'd expect `rec 2/19`, not `rec 1/19`. So free-running-clock death is a strong suspect but not proven, and I'm not going to tell you it's solved when the arithmetic has a gap in it.

That shapes b71 — it carries the fix *and* the instrumentation to adjudicate it:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""b71 - three changes, all aimed at the boot-time I2S RX stall.

1. voice/mic.c  - requeue the TX silence buffer instead of letting it drain.
2. voice/mic.c  - per-ioctl stage markers inside mic_session_close().
3. ui/ui_lvgl.c - a failed capture no longer disables voice for the boot.

Writes <file>.new and os.replace()s it.  Asserts every prior-state marker
first, so a re-run or a drifted tree aborts instead of half-applying.
"""

import io
import os
import sys

APP = r"D:\openVela\contest2026_043_CircuitForge\app\velapaw"
MIC = os.path.join(APP, "voice", "mic.c")
UI = os.path.join(APP, "ui", "ui_lvgl.c")


def read(path, minlen):
    with io.open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        s = f.read()
    if len(s) < minlen:
        sys.exit("ABORT: %s is %d bytes, expected >= %d" % (path, len(s), minlen))
    return s


def sub(s, old, new, what):
    n = s.count(old)
    if n != 1:
        sys.exit("ABORT: %s -- anchor found %d times, expected 1" % (what, n))
    return s.replace(old, new, 1)


def write(path, s):
    tmp = path + ".new"
    with io.open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        f.write(s)
    os.replace(tmp, path)
    print("  wrote %s (%d bytes)" % (path, len(s)))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- mic.c ----

m = read(MIC, 40000)

for marker in ('"session-close",     /* 32 */',
               "#define MIC_STAGE_DONE       33",
               "static void mic_session_close(struct mic_ctx_s *ctx)",
               "          if (apb == ctx->playbuf)"):
    if marker not in m:
        sys.exit("ABORT: mic.c missing expected marker: %r" % marker)

if "MIC_STAGE_CL_STOP_REC" in m:
    sys.exit("ABORT: mic.c already patched (MIC_STAGE_CL_STOP_REC present)")

# -- 1. stage name table ----------------------------------------------------

m = sub(m,
        '  "done"               /* 33 */\n};',
        '  "done",              /* 33 */\n'
        '\n'
        '  /* Close sub-stages.  These sit after "done" because the numbers are\n'
        '   * an append-only wire format -- the probe output is read against\n'
        '   * notes taken on earlier builds, so renumbering 0-33 to make the\n'
        '   * ordering pretty would silently invalidate every one of them.\n'
        '   */\n'
        '\n'
        '  "cl-stop-rec",       /* 34 */\n'
        '  "cl-stop-play",      /* 35 */\n'
        '  "cl-quiesce",        /* 36 */\n'
        '  "cl-unregister-mq",  /* 37 */\n'
        '  "cl-free-rec-bufs",  /* 38 */\n'
        '  "cl-free-play-buf",  /* 39 */\n'
        '  "cl-release",        /* 40 */\n'
        '  "cl-close-fds"       /* 41 */\n'
        '};',
        "mic.c stage name table")

# -- 2. stage constants -----------------------------------------------------

m = sub(m,
        "#define MIC_STAGE_DONE       33\n",
        "#define MIC_STAGE_DONE       33\n"
        "\n"
        "/* Inside mic_session_close().  Stage 32 used to cover two AUDIOIOC_STOPs,\n"
        " * the quiesce, UNREGISTERMQ, 19 FREEBUFFERs, two RELEASEs and two close()s\n"
        " * with no marker between them, so a hang anywhere in the teardown reported\n"
        " * the same number.  ps showed the worker in `Waiting Semaphore`, which says\n"
        " * it is blocked in a driver call but not which one; these say which one.\n"
        " */\n"
        "\n"
        "#define MIC_STAGE_CL_STOP_REC  34\n"
        "#define MIC_STAGE_CL_STOP_PLY  35\n"
        "#define MIC_STAGE_CL_QUIESCE   36\n"
        "#define MIC_STAGE_CL_UNREGMQ   37\n"
        "#define MIC_STAGE_CL_FREE_REC  38\n"
        "#define MIC_STAGE_CL_FREE_PLY  39\n"
        "#define MIC_STAGE_CL_RELEASE   40\n"
        "#define MIC_STAGE_CL_CLOSEFD   41\n",
        "mic.c stage constants")

# -- 3. markers inside mic_session_close() ----------------------------------

m = sub(m,
        "  if (ctx->rec_started)\n"
        "    {\n"
        "      ioctl(ctx->recfd, AUDIOIOC_STOP, 0);\n"
        "    }\n"
        "\n"
        "  if (ctx->play_started)\n"
        "    {\n"
        "      ioctl(ctx->playfd, AUDIOIOC_STOP, 0);\n"
        "    }\n",
        "  if (ctx->rec_started)\n"
        "    {\n"
        "      MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_CL_STOP_REC);\n"
        "      ioctl(ctx->recfd, AUDIOIOC_STOP, 0);\n"
        "    }\n"
        "\n"
        "  if (ctx->play_started)\n"
        "    {\n"
        "      MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_CL_STOP_PLY);\n"
        "      ioctl(ctx->playfd, AUDIOIOC_STOP, 0);\n"
        "    }\n",
        "mic.c close: STOP markers")

m = sub(m,
        "  mic_quiesce(ctx);\n",
        "  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_CL_QUIESCE);\n"
        "  mic_quiesce(ctx);\n",
        "mic.c close: quiesce marker")

m = sub(m,
        "  if (ctx->mq_open)\n"
        "    {\n"
        "      if (ctx->recfd >= 0)\n"
        "        {\n"
        "          ioctl(ctx->recfd, AUDIOIOC_UNREGISTERMQ, (unsigned long)ctx->mq);\n",
        "  if (ctx->mq_open)\n"
        "    {\n"
        "      MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_CL_UNREGMQ);\n"
        "\n"
        "      if (ctx->recfd >= 0)\n"
        "        {\n"
        "          ioctl(ctx->recfd, AUDIOIOC_UNREGISTERMQ, (unsigned long)ctx->mq);\n",
        "mic.c close: unregister-mq marker")

m = sub(m,
        "  for (i = 0; i < ctx->nrecbufs; i++)\n"
        "    {\n"
        "      if (ctx->recbufs[i] != NULL)\n",
        "  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_CL_FREE_REC);\n"
        "\n"
        "  for (i = 0; i < ctx->nrecbufs; i++)\n"
        "    {\n"
        "      if (ctx->recbufs[i] != NULL)\n",
        "mic.c close: free-rec marker")

m = sub(m,
        "  if (ctx->playbuf != NULL)\n"
        "    {\n"
        "      memset(&desc, 0, sizeof(desc));\n",
        "  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_CL_FREE_PLY);\n"
        "\n"
        "  if (ctx->playbuf != NULL)\n"
        "    {\n"
        "      memset(&desc, 0, sizeof(desc));\n",
        "mic.c close: free-play marker")

m = sub(m,
        "  if (ctx->rec_reserved)\n"
        "    {\n"
        "      ioctl(ctx->recfd, AUDIOIOC_RELEASE, 0);\n",
        "  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_CL_RELEASE);\n"
        "\n"
        "  if (ctx->rec_reserved)\n"
        "    {\n"
        "      ioctl(ctx->recfd, AUDIOIOC_RELEASE, 0);\n",
        "mic.c close: release marker")

m = sub(m,
        "  if (ctx->recfd >= 0)\n"
        "    {\n"
        "      close(ctx->recfd);\n",
        "  MIC_STAGE(MIC_STAGE_CL_CLOSEFD);\n"
        "\n"
        "  if (ctx->recfd >= 0)\n"
        "    {\n"
        "      close(ctx->recfd);\n",
        "mic.c close: close-fd marker")

# -- 4. requeue TX ----------------------------------------------------------

m = sub(m,
        "          /* A playback buffer coming back is the primed silence completing.\n"
        "           * Do not treat it as captured audio -- and do not requeue it, so\n"
        "           * TX stays quiet while RX keeps the clock it already has.\n"
        "           */\n"
        "\n"
        "          if (apb == ctx->playbuf)\n"
        "            {\n"
        "              continue;\n"
        "            }\n",

        "          /* A playback buffer coming back is the primed silence completing.\n"
        "           * It is not captured audio, so it never joins `out` -- but it IS\n"
        "           * re-primed, which is a reversal of what this code used to do.\n"
        "           *\n"

**What b71 changes, and what it will tell us**

To be straight about the state of this: your directive was to check the priority, and I did — `ps` rules it out with evidence rather than opinion. Everything in group 4 sits at 100, the es8311 workers sit at 252 parked on an *empty* queue, and nothing is blocked on a lock held by something slower. The high-priority threads aren't being starved; they have no work because the I²S driver stopped handing them buffers. So b71 goes after the thing that stopped, not the threads that were waiting on it.

The substantive change is deleting an assumption. `mic_arm()` primes TX with one 256 ms buffer of silence and, until now, `mic_collect()` deliberately threw that buffer away when it came back — trusting patch #16 to keep BCLK/WS free-running on an empty FIFO for the remaining ~750 ms of every capture. RX has no clock of its own on this part; it borrows TX's. That assumption was never measured, only inferred from captures that worked, and `play 1/1` in all three failing dumps is precisely what it looks like when it doesn't hold. TX now gets re-primed each time it completes.

**But I'm not claiming this is the fix.** The arithmetic has a gap I flagged before writing the patch and it hasn't closed: one RX buffer is ~128 ms, so RX died at ~128 ms while TX still had ~128 ms of silence left to clock out. A clock that merely ran dry at 256 ms should have produced `rec 2/19`. That's why b71 carries instrumentation alongside the fix rather than betting on it.

Three readings to expect from the next failing boot, if it still fails:

- **`play` head climbing (4/4, 8/8, …)** — TX stayed fed and the clock theory is dead. The stall is in the RX DMA descriptor chain, and I'd want the VM's `esp32s3_i2s.c` next.
- **`play 1/1` still** — the requeue never ran, meaning we never got the completion message back, which relocates the problem earlier than I've been looking.
- **`mic stage` now 34–41 instead of 32** — names exactly which teardown ioctl `Waiting Semaphore` is parked in. Stage 34/35 would confirm my `AUDIOIOC_STOP` suspicion; 36 would mean the quiesce (though it's bounded at 4 s and shouldn't hang); 38 would mean a FREEBUFFER on a buffer the driver still holds.

The third change is unrelated to the root cause and I want to be clear it's a mitigation, not a fix: one failed capture used to latch `g_voice_fail` and park the thread, killing voice until the next power cycle. It now retries up to 4 times with fresh sessions. That only helps a capture that *returns* an error — the current stall hangs inside `velapaw_mic_capture()` and never returns, so it won't rescue this particular bug. It removes the second, avoidable way voice dies, not the first.

Test rule still applies: **cold power cycle, then straight to `velapaw voice`.** No `velapaw kws mic` first.

— the voice dialog being open, or **the Recognize tab being on screen**. The board boots on Enroll (tab 0), so the mic has never been asked to run. `caps 0` with `mic stage 0 (idle)` and `mic open none yet` is the correct idle state, not a result.

That also retroactively explains the earlier failures: `caps 1` in those boots was the first capture triggered by the board *sitting on the Recognize tab*. The stall was always the first capture after landing on that tab.

So, on the device screen:

1. **Tap the Recognize tab.**
2. Leave it there ~10 seconds so the worker gets several capture attempts.
3. Back at the console: `velapaw voice`

What to look for, unchanged from before:

- **`caps` climbing, `lastret 0`, `ready 1`** — fixed. Re-priming TX was the answer.
- **Stalled with `play` head at 4/4 or higher** — TX stayed fed; the clock theory is dead and the stall is in the RX DMA chain. The `mic stage` will be 34–41 naming the exact teardown ioctl.
- **Stalled with `play 1/1`** — the requeue never ran; the playback completion never came back to us at all.

One thing this boot does establish for free: nothing is wedged. `stage 0`, `lasterr 0`, no stale `-110`. The cold power cycle gave us a genuinely clean slate, so whatever comes back next is the first capture on fresh hardware state with the fix in place.

The instrumentation paid off. **`mic stage 34 (cl-stop-rec)`** — the hang is in the very first ioctl of the teardown:

```c
ioctl(ctx->recfd, AUDIOIOC_STOP, 0);   /* record device — never returns */
```

That's stage 32's blind spot resolved to a single line, and it confirms the suspicion I'd flagged as unproven: it *is* the first `AUDIOIOC_STOP`, on the record side. `seq 46` fits exactly — 45 was `CLOSE`, 46 is `CL_STOP_REC`, so it entered teardown and died immediately.

Combined with the `ps` you took earlier, the causal chain now closes:

- RX stalled with 18 buffers still sitting in es8311's pending queue (`rec 1/19` — 19 handed over, 1 came back).
- The es8311 worker won't terminate while it still holds outstanding buffers, which is why `ps` showed it `Waiting MQ empty` — alive, waiting on DMA completions that will never arrive.
- `AUDIOIOC_STOP` on the record device joins that worker. It blocks forever. Our thread shows `Waiting Semaphore`. `g_mic_busy` never clears, so every later caller gets `-EBUSY`.

So the close hang is fully explained as a *consequence*. The root cause is unchanged and unmoved: **RX DMA stops after exactly one buffer.**

Now the part that goes against my hypothesis. **`play 1/1` — the TX requeue never ran.** That's outcome 3, the one I said would most change my mind, so let me be straight about what it does to the theory rather than salvage it. The re-prime code sits in `mic_collect()` and only fires when the playback completion message arrives; it never fired. And the arithmetic that already bothered me now bites harder: TX reports one completed buffer, but 8192 bytes at 16 kHz is 256 ms of clock, which should have yielded ~2 RX buffers, not 1. The single RX buffer that did come back was **all zeros** (`phase -1`).

One completed TX buffer plus one empty RX buffer plus no clock is not "the clock ran dry mid-capture". It looks like **the clock never really started** — TX completed its buffer without clocking it out, and RX returned its first descriptor empty. Re-priming TX can't fix a TX that isn't transmitting. My free-running-clock theory addressed the wrong half of the window.

The fix isn't harmful and the instrumentation is worth keeping, but I'm not going to call it a fix. I need the driver now.

Line 1046 settles it. The **TX** path in the same file walks correctly:

```c
while (!(bfdesc->ctrl & ESP32S3_DMA_CTRL_EOF))    /* find the desc carrying EOF */
    bfdesc = bfdesc->next;
```

The **RX** path uses a different and wrong idiom — it advances only while the *next* descriptor has EOF, so it stops at `d[0]` on any chain where EOF isn't on `d[1]`, hands back the wrong pointer, fails the `==` test, and silently wedges. Two implementations of the same walk, in one file, disagreeing.

Let me check the worker's EOF handling before writing the patch.

Conclusive — and your own patch #10 proves it. At [vm-esp32s3_i2s.c:1424](C:/Users/VICTUS/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Users-VICTUS-openVela/3659500b-38f3-47db-bbd0-9b2aab159cd9/scratchpad/vm-esp32s3_i2s.c#L1424):

> *"VelaPaw patch #10: the loop condition tested EOF on every link, but the hardware sets suc_eof only on the LAST descriptor of a chain. On any multi-descriptor transfer it therefore exited on d[0]..."*

The upstream driver has that same broken walk in **two** places. Patch #10 fixed it in `i2s_rx_worker` and **missed the copy in `i2s_rx_schedule`**. That surviving copy is what's wedging RX.

And the missing `else` is flagged by upstream itself, at line 1036 in the TX twin:

> *"REVISIT: what to do if we miss syncronization and the descriptor that generated the interrupt is different from the expected"*

Nobody ever answered that REVISIT. The answer, on RX, is "hang forever and require a power cycle."


The script refuses to apply unless the file is the exact revision I analysed — size in range, patch #10 present, patch #31 absent, and both code anchors matching once. I dry-ran all of it against your actual file and every check passes.

---

**What was wrong**

`i2s_rx_schedule()` in [esp32s3_i2s.c:1139](C:/Users/VICTUS/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Users-VICTUS-openVela/3659500b-38f3-47db-bbd0-9b2aab159cd9/scratchpad/vm-esp32s3_i2s.c#L1139) walks the DMA chain looking for the descriptor that raised EOF, but advances only while the *next* link has EOF. The hardware sets `suc_eof` on the **last** descriptor, so on a multi-descriptor transfer the walk stops at `d[0]`, compares it against an `inlink` pointing at `d[n]`, and the comparison fails. There's no `else`. The buffer stays in `rx.act`; `i2s_rxdma_start()` sees a non-empty `rx.act`, concludes a transfer is already running, and returns. RX is dead, permanently, with every later buffer piling up in `rx.pend`.

That is `rec 1/19` exactly: one completion got through, the second desynced, eighteen stranded.

The rest was consequence. es8311's worker can't terminate holding stranded buffers, so `AUDIOIOC_STOP` joins it and blocks — **stage 34**, which is why that marker was worth adding. `g_mic_busy` never clears, so voice stays dead until a power cycle.

You had already fixed this exact bug once. Patch #10's comment says it outright: *"the hardware sets suc_eof only on the LAST descriptor of a chain."* It fixed `i2s_rx_worker()`. The identical broken walk in `i2s_rx_schedule()` was missed. The TX twin at line 1046 walks correctly and always has.

The patch does two things: corrects the walk to match TX and patch #10, and supplies the missing `else` — which is upstream's own unanswered *"REVISIT: what to do if we miss syncronization"*. On RX the answer matters, because doing nothing costs the entire stream until a power cycle. A mismatch now completes the head buffer and restarts DMA, and bumps `g_i2s_rx_desync` so we can tell whether the recovery is load-bearing or just insurance. No logging in that path — it's ISR context, where syslog faults on this part.

**Two corrections to things I told you earlier in this session.** The TX free-running-clock theory was wrong; re-priming TX in b71 addressed a window that was never the problem, and `play 1/1` was the signal that should have moved me off it sooner than it did. And my first instruction to just run `velapaw voice` was wrong — that's a probe, it arms nothing; the Recognize tab is what starts capture.

b71's other two changes stay and are still worth having: the close-path stage markers are what located this, and the non-terminal capture failure means a future stall degrades instead of killing voice for the boot.

**Cold power cycle** — full unplug/replug, not a RESET tap.

Then on the device screen: **tap the Recognize tab**, leave it ~10 seconds, and back at the console:

```bash
py -m serial.tools.miniterm COM4 115200
```
